case_title: Shiv Shankar Prasad Singh v. The State of Bihar
accused_occupation: Government employee of the Food Corporation of India depot: AG-III (in charge of receipt of consignments) for Shiv Shankar Prasad Singh; Depot Incharge for Ramdeo Prasad
accused_victim_relationship: Employees of the complainant organisation (Food Corporation of India); co-workers at the depot
statutory_provisions: IPC s.409, s.477A, s.120B r/w s.409 and s.477A; Prevention of Corruption Act 1947 s.5(2) r/w s.5(1)(c) and (d)
evidence_type: Documentary (gate register, arrival tally book, G and O Form registers, delivery book, gate passes, Ext.24 chart) and oral (truck owners, drivers, cleaner, FCI officers, document examiner, investigating officer)
aggravating_circumstances: Falsification of official FCI records to conceal misappropriation of 1040 bags of urea; conspiracy among accused
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.120B r/w s.409 and s.477A IPC and s.5(1)(d) PC Act (punishable under s.5(2)); RI 3 years under s.409 IPC, RI 3 years under s.477A (for Ramdeo Prasad), RI 2 years and fine Rs.10,000 under s.5(1)(c)/(d) PC Act
high_court_outcome: Appeals dismissed; conviction confirmed; sentences reduced (Shiv Shankar Prasad Singh: RI 6 months under s.120B r/w s.409, RI 6 months under s.477A, RI 6 months and fine Rs.15,000 under s.5(1)(d) r/w s.5(2) PC Act)
offence_finally_established: Criminal conspiracy (s.120B r/w s.409 IPC), s.477A IPC, and s.5(1)(d) PC Act (s.5(2)) for Shiv Shankar Prasad Singh; s.409 and s.477A IPC and s.5(1)(c) PC Act (s.5(2)) for Ramdeo Prasad
neutral_facts: The victim organisation, a food corporation, alleged that a depot in-charge and other staff conspired with a transporter and a contractor to misappropriate urea fertiliser bags during March 1980. A complaint dated December 1981 led to registration of a first information report, which initially referred to 540 bags. Wagons carrying fertiliser were placed at a railway station for unloading, and delivery was signed for in the delivery book on 24 and 25 March 1980. The prosecution alleged that 500 bags were handed over to a representative who signed gate passes for two trucks, each said to carry 250 bags to the depot. The accused responsible for receipt at the depot gate register and the in-charge who maintained the godown registers were said to have entered the arrival of these bags, although the bags were never delivered. The investigation concluded that the entire 1040 bags were misappropriated. Evidence included depositions of the two truck owners, the drivers and a cleaner, who stated that one truck was diverted to a different location and the other was never used for carrying fertiliser. The gate register, arrival tally book, daily receipt register and godown stock register were examined, together with a chart prepared in October 1982 showing delivery of the 500 bags. A government document examiner, an audit assistant manager, a physical verification officer and the investigating officer also testified. Defence evidence came from a retired assistant depot manager.
number_of_offences: 5 charged (IPC s.409, s.477A, s.120B; PC Act s.5(1)(c), s.5(1)(d)); 5 finally upheld across both appellants (Shiv Shankar Prasad Singh: s.120B r/w s.409, s.477A, s.5(1)(d); Ramdeo Prasad: s.409, s.477A, s.5(1)(c))
financial_property_loss: Misappropriation of 1040 bags of urea (monetary value not stated)
premeditation_planning: Yes: the court accepted a conspiracy with criminal intent and falsification of accounts across the accused
motive: alleged: misappropriation of fertiliser bags with criminal intent
key_evidence_accepted: Depositions of truck owners, drivers and cleaner (PW-9, PW-10, PW-14, PW-15, PW-18) that the 500 bags were not delivered; one truck diverted to Manjhaul and the other never used for fertiliser; investigating officer's deposition (PW-21); falsified gate, G Form and O Form registers
witness_credibility: Owner, driver and cleaner testimony found positive and reliable and rightly relied on; Ext.24 chart and evidence of PW-4 and PW-20 discounted because the chart was prepared much after the FIR
bail_history: Bail bonds cancelled by the Supreme Court; appellants directed to surrender within four weeks
trial_duration: offence: March 1980 (complaint dated 23.12.1981); trial judgment: 26.09.1997; High Court: 17.02.2009; Supreme Court: 28.02.2019
legal_representation: Appellants: Santosh Mishra, Manish Kumar, Ms. Sharmila Upadhyay, Ms. Aparajita Singh, T. Mahipal (Advocates). State/CBI: P. K. Dey, A. K. Srivastava, Arvind Kumar Sharma, Ashok Kumar Srivastava (Advocates)
investigation_status: FIR registered on complaint; investigation by CBI (investigating officer PW-21); chargesheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court (Special Judge CBI, Patna): convicted and sentenced. High Court: conviction confirmed, sentences reduced. Supreme Court: appeals dismissed, bail bonds cancelled, surrender ordered.
prosecution_argument: Initial complaint covered 540 bags but investigation showed all 1040 bags misappropriated; false entries in gate register, G Form and O Form; evidence consistent; conspiracy proved beyond reasonable doubt; concurrent findings not perverse and should not be disturbed
defence_argument: FIR concerned only 540 bags; truck witnesses inconsistent and contradictory; trial and appellate courts should not have relied on transport evidence; PW-4 and PW-20 and Ext.24 show 500 bags reached the godown; audit report supports receipt
legal_principle_applied: Totality of oral and documentary evidence assessed for proof beyond reasonable doubt; concurrent findings not interfered with unless perverse or erroneous
sentencing_rationale: Not applicable: appeals dismissed and remaining High Court sentence ordered to be served; no separate sentencing reasoning given
judicial_aggravating_factors: Conspiracy among all accused and falsification of FCI records, weighed in confirming the findings
other_sentence_order: Bail bonds cancelled; surrender within four weeks; failing surrender, respondents may take necessary steps against the accused
